punchline: The best photographs came from the students graded on how many they made.
thirty_sec: A photography teacher split his class into two groups. One earned grades by producing more pictures; the other needed one nearly perfect photograph. In James Clear's telling, the quantity students experimented and learned from mistakes while the quality students discussed perfection. At the end, the best photographs came from the quantity group. They had spent their time practicing the skill their work was supposed to demonstrate.
question: What did making your first attempt teach you that preparation hadn't?
